ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.46 rolls up ban enforcement, bot detection, and CLI ad
ai.summary: Version 0.0.46 packages the April 22-23 changes that harden Freebuff's free-tier abuse handling: sessions now return HTTP 403 for banned users and flip to a country_blocked terminal state on free_mode_unavailable, the agent runtime parses stringified tool-call input before Zod validation, and the CLI waiting room renders Carbon ads via the unified ChoiceAdBanner component. Server-side, a new /api/admin/bot-sweep endpoint plus abuse-detection refinements (quiet-gap window clipping, region signals, GitHub account age counter-weights, and TIER 1 tightening) feed manual review flows. Packaging metadata updates only; functional changes live in freebuff/cli and web/session services.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in freebuff/cli/release/package.json changes "version" from "0.0.45" to "0.0.46"; analysis notes confirm this release-bump rolls up user-visible features, model changes, and CLI improvements shipped since 0.0.45, including the bot-sweep endpoint, 403 ban rejection, abuse scoring refinements, Carbon CLI ads, choice-banner UI, country-block terminal state, quiet-gap SQL fix, and region-signal heuristic.

eli5.text: This update sharpens Freebuff's ability to catch abusive bots and unfairly bans suspicious accounts while protecting legitimate long-time users from false flags. If you get flagged wrongly, the system now checks how established your account is before taking action, and banned users are blocked from joining the queue entirely. The waiting room now shows ads from a new provider (Carbon) and renders all ads through a unified, cleaner banner, giving you clearer choices about what you see. Freebuff also recovers from certain payment or regional issues more gracefully, freeing up your queue slot instead of freezing, and it shows the project picker up front so you always pick your folder before logging in. Upgrading means a fairer, more stable experience with fewer interruptions and cleaner ad displays.

ai.title: Add deployment hours availability for GLM 5.1 and MiniMax M2.7 support
ai.summary: GLM 5.1 (`z-ai/glm-5.1`) availability is restricted to deployment hours (9am ET-5pm PT) via new `availability` policy in `FREEBUFF_MODELS`. MiniMax M2.7 (`minimax/minimax-m2.7`) added as always-available option and mapped in `createCodeEditor`. CLI model store resolves available models; session hook handles `model_unavailable` 409s by resetting to default. `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` variants removed from `ModelName`.

eli5.text: If you open the free assistant in the CLI between 9am Eastern and 5pm Pacific on a weekday, you can now pick the GLM 5.1 model; outside those hours it stays dimmed out. At the same time, MiniMax M2.7 has been added as a model you can choose at any time, and the older kimi-k2.5 variants have been removed from the list of models shown in the free assistant. When you try to join the queue for a model that isn't available right now, the interface now tells you that plainly instead of erroring out, and you'll be guided back to the default model. The change is live today for anyone using the free tier of the CLI.

ai.title: GLM rate limit 5 sessions per 20 hours
ai.summary: Added per-model session quota for GLM 5.1 (5 admits per 20h window). New `rate_limited` status in CLI `WaitingRoomScreen` shows usage and retry time. DB migration `0046` creates `free_session_admit` table with index on user/model/time. API returns 429 on POST when quota exceeded; older CLIs back off due to status code.

eli5.text: If you use the free GLM 5.1 assistant in the CLI and have already started 5 sessions in the past 20 hours, the app will now show a waiting screen that tells you roughly when you can try again, for example "in ~45 min", instead of silently refusing or polling repeatedly. The limit is enforced server-side: your sixth attempt in that window is turned away with a clear message and a count of how many of your 5 allowed sessions have been used. Older CLI versions that don\'t recognize the new message will simply back off and retry later, since the server signals the pause with a standard rate-limit status code. This only applies to GLM 5.1; other models in the free tier are unaffected.

ai.title: CLI ad system adds Carbon fallback for Gravity
ai.summary: The `useGravityAd` hook now accepts a `fallbackProvider` option and iterates through a list of providers if the primary fails or returns no fill. This change updates `chat.tsx` and `waiting-room-screen.tsx` to specify `gravity` as the primary provider and `carbon` as the fallback, replacing the previous behavior where the waiting room exclusively used Carbon. The mechanism ensures ad continuity in the CLI by attempting a secondary network when the first is unavailable.

eli5.text: When you open the app and there's no conversation yet, the waiting room now tries one ad network first and, if that can't find an ad to show, automatically tries a second one so you're not left looking at a blank spot. This affects anyone who uses the free tier or lands in the waiting room before their chat starts, you'll just see an ad load instead of a gap, with no action needed on your part. The new double-check behavior is already live.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI release package version bumped to 0.0.47
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package version has been bumped from 0.0.46 to 0.0.47, bundling the prior day's three notable and minor updates into a single packaged release. This version increment follows 0.0.46 (a minor release that also only updated the same package.json file) and precedes a later bump to 0.0.48. The change is a pure metadata update with no code logic modified in this commit, serving to publish previously merged features and fixes to consumers of the `freebuff` CLI npm package.
ai.evidence: Commit 4bed3c79 increments the `version` field from 0.0.46 to 0.0.47 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, the sole file modified in this release-bump commit.

eli5.text: Version 0.0.47 adds two new AI models you can work with, plus a smarter way to handle busy or unavailable model access, and a smoother ad fallback system. You now have access to MiniMax M2, a newer model that is always available, while Z AI's GLM 5.1 is available only during certain hours (9am Eastern to 5pm Pacific) and limited to five sessions every twenty hours, with the command line showing you a clear message and retry time if you hit that limit. When a model is temporarily unavailable due to these new usage policies, your tool automatically switches you back to the default model so your workflow keeps moving instead of getting stuck. The in terminal ad system that can help support the service is also more reliable, since it now falls back to a second ad provider if the first one is not available, which means fewer blank or broken ad spots while you wait. Upgrading gives you access to the latest model options, clearer messages when models are busy, and a more consistent experience overall.

ai.title: Add fallback model ID
ai.summary: Added `FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID` constant and `FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_MODEL_ID` to `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`. `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID` now points to GLM, while fallback logic in `useFreebuffSession` and `freebuff-model-store` uses the always-available MiniMax model. `setSelectedModel` in `freebuff-model-store.ts` is now in-memory only, moving persistence exclusively to `joinFreebuffQueue` in `use-freebuff-session.ts` to prevent server-driven auto-flips from overwriting user preferences.

eli5.text: When you're picking which assistant model to use in the CLI, the app now makes sure you can always actually get one -- even if your preferred choice (GLM) is temporarily unavailable due to its scheduled hours. Instead of silently flipping you over and then 'remembering' that fallback forever, it keeps the switch in memory for this session only so your real preference stays saved for next time. The fallback model it lands on is MiniMax M2.7, which is marked as 'always available.' This is now live behavior in the model picker and session joining flow.

ai.title: Freebuff version 0.0.48 released in CLI package manifest
ai.summary: The version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from 0.0.47 to 0.0.48. This release-bump commit follows the 0.0.47 version bump and ships alongside earlier work including the fallback model ID addition (FALLBACK_FREEBUFF_MODEL_ID pointing to MiniMax) and GLM 5.1 deployment hour restrictions. The change affects the CLI package manifest only; this release bundles the fallback model routing logic, MiniMax M2.7 support, and GLM rate limiting changes from the preceding commits.
ai.evidence: Commit 8bc9c342 modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `0.0.47` to `0.0.48`. This is a release-bump commit following the 0.0.47 bump in commit 4bed3c79, with no functional code changes in the diff itself.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.48 brings smarter, more reliable AI model selection so you always have a working assistant even when your first-choice AI model isn't available. The default AI model has switched to GLM, but a fallback MiniMax model now kicks in automatically if GLM is unreachable, preventing interruptions during your coding sessions. Your personal model preferences are now saved more carefully, meaning the system won't override your chosen AI model with automatic switches, but your selections stay consistent across restarts. Upgrading means fewer surprises from unexpected model changes and a smoother experience when some AI options are temporarily offline.
